messages:
maria (support): FYI customer AcmeHealth reporting streaming sessions getting cut + duplicated billing. They see partial outputs then reconnects and a sharp token/usage spike. Logs attached below.

acme_health (customer): repro steps: open SSE stream, token expires after ~5m, client hits 401 and immediately refreshes token and re-opens stream. After that sometimes we receive duplicate/missing chunks and our usage meter doubled for the same user.

kai (oncall): thanks. can you paste the minimal client flow you use for token refresh + reconnect? also any request ids/stream ids we can look up on server logs?

acme_health (customer): client is simple fetch SSE, refresh on 401, code:
```
const evtSource = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
// on 401 -> getNewToken(); open new fetch immediately
```
We do not explicitly close old connection before opening new one.

devon (eng-runtime): that pattern can cause overlapping streams. on our side we treat each incoming connection as a separate billing session. if a token refresh opens a second stream without closing the first, both are counted. can you share a trace id?

maria (support): trace id 3f2b7a1c, connection ids in logs: conn-9182, conn-9183. server log snippet: 
```
[2024-11-12T12:04:09Z] conn-9182 START_STREAM user=acme:user42 trace=3f2b7a1c
[2024-11-12T12:09:18Z] conn-9182 AUTH_FAILURE token_expired
[2024-11-12T12:09:19Z] conn-9183 START_STREAM user=acme:user42 trace=3f2b7a1c
[2024-11-12T12:09:19Z] conn-9182 STILL_ACTIVE chunks_sent=3
```
We see conn-9182 didn't get a server-side close before conn-9183 started.

ashley (devex): couple of notes: some intermediary proxies (ALBs, corporate proxies) silently close idle TCP without passing SSE comment pings, so clients think stream is alive and try to refresh token -> open new. ALB idle timeout defaults to 60s, most browsers don't expose low-level TCP keepalive. Workarounds: 1) client sends SSE comment pings `: keepalive\n\n` every 15s, 2) use a short reconnect backoff + explicit close before refresh, 3) use Last-Event-ID and server-side idempotency header. Also customer-side: if you refresh token, close old source first (`evtSource.close()`) then open new one.

billing-bot: ALERT: customer acme_health observed 2.1x token usage increase over 30m window; spike triggered billing alert #B-7742.

kai (oncall): short-term mitigation: server can accept a `x-client-stream-id` header and treat new connections with same id as replacement for the older one within a grace window (5s). longer-term: implement server-side dedupe/soft-close and better accounting (attribute overlapping window to single session).

devon (eng-runtime): agreed. i'll prototype: when new stream arrives with same `x-client-stream-id` mark existing connection as "replaced" and send an SSE event `event: replaced\ndata: reason=token-refresh\n\n` then stop billing for the old one after drain. canary on dedicated cluster + telemetry to ensure we don't silently drop legitimate parallel streams.

maria (support): i'll pass workaround to customer (close before refresh + comment pings) and open an internal RFC for server dedupe. will link to billing alert and attach the trace + logs. thank you :tada:
